limits: External sources support only the named mechanism; transfers and local suitability are engineering recommendations, not measured PolicyOS guarantees. Local authority documents retain their own status.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.supported_claim: ETag identifies and validates a selected representation; If-None-Match can produce 304; 304 carries no representation body; Range/206 is optional and If-Range must use a strong matching validator; HTTP idempotence concerns intended server effect, and clients should not automatically retry a non-idempotent request without a means to know it is safe or detect non-application.
sources.limits: HTTP validators are origin assertions about a representation, not cryptographic content hashes, snapshot completeness proofs, rights decisions, or current legal status.

sources.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
sources.supported_claim: Cache reuse depends on target, method, freshness or successful revalidation, and Vary-selected request fields; a 304 updates an appropriate stored response, and partial responses require matching representation validators before combination.
sources.limits: The HTTP cache model does not admit a PolicyOS use, prove source authority, or ensure that a source's paged records form a stable semantic snapshot.

sources.title: RFC 8288: Web Linking
sources.supported_claim: The Link header models typed relations between a current context and target resources and defines parsing and relative-target resolution semantics.
sources.limits: A next-like relation is a navigation hint/protocol value, not proof that all pages share a consistent source cut or permission. Every dereference still needs the selected transport and egress policy.

sources.title: OWASP Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supported_claim: For known destinations, accept a host from an allowlist and construct the request locally; validate resolved IPv4 and IPv6 targets and bind the connection to an approved address because a separate DNS check does not prevent rebinding; redirects and parser disagreement must not bypass destination checks.
sources.limits: This is defensive guidance, not a proof of the repository's proxy, DNS, socket, or firewall behavior; those enforcement points must be verified for the selected deployment.

sources.title: Use delta query to track changes in Microsoft Graph data
sources.supported_claim: Graph's opaque nextLink and deltaLink tokens represent state for a change-tracking round; clients continue until deltaLink, preserve query state, and must handle duplicate/replayed items, processing delay, and expired tokens requiring resynchronization.
sources.limits: This is one provider's API contract. It documents that some resource properties outside the main store are not tracked, so a delta feed cannot be generalized into a complete change denominator for other sources.

sources.title: How to prevent object overwrites with conditional writes
sources.supported_claim: S3 supports conditional object writes using If-Match/If-None-Match, rejecting mismatched versions with precondition/conflict responses; this is a concrete compare-and-swap pattern for a selected object head.
sources.limits: Provider behavior and multipart/delete races are S3-specific; this is a mechanism comparison, not a recommendation to add S3 or evidence of filesystem/CAS parity.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.supported_claim: ODRL supplies an interoperable model for asset-linked permissions, prohibitions, duties, parties, and constraints, useful as an input vocabulary for purpose/use evidence.
sources.limits: An ODRL expression can state a policy but does not authenticate its issuer, establish signer competence, decide legal force, or prove that a custodian granted the asserted permission.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.supported_claim: PROV-O separates entities, activities, and agents and connects used/generated entities with responsible agents and times, a useful reference for capture and transformation provenance.
sources.limits: A provenance graph records asserted relationships; it does not make an agent's assertion true or supply authority, permission, or verification.

sources.title: Verify the authenticity of an electronic edition of the Official Journal
sources.source_kind: EU Publications Office first-party legal-source guidance
sources.supported_claim: For the EU Official Journal, the electronic edition is the authentic legally effective edition from 1 July 2013, and its signature-verification procedure checks that the signed edition is authentic and unchanged since signature.
sources.limits: This route is specific to the Official Journal and the applicable EU legal rule. It does not make every EUR-Lex page, consolidation, translation, or linked record independently authoritative.

sources.title: What is ELI?
sources.supported_claim: ELI offers persistent identifiers and a common metadata model for legislation, including identifiers and descriptive/version information that support machine-readable legal-source discovery and citation.
sources.limits: An identifier or metadata record does not prove the authenticity of the fetched bytes, current legal effect, jurisdictional applicability, or an institution's interpretation.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (consolidated text)
sources.supported_claim: The regulation defines electronic seals as linked to origin/integrity and gives qualified seals specified evidentiary presumptions; it also defines qualified timestamp and trust-service semantics.
sources.limits: The specific legal effect depends on the applicable legal regime and trust chain. A verified seal alone does not establish that the signer had authority to issue the legal act or that the act applies to a target policy question.

sources.title: Authentication and the 2026 Code of Federal Regulations
sources.source_kind: U.S. Government Publishing Office first-party publication guidance
sources.supported_claim: GovInfo's digitally signed publications support verification of certification, integrity, and signer identity at signing; its CFR documentation directs users to the Federal Register and List of CFR Sections Affected to identify amendments and warns that publication and effective dates differ.
sources.limits: This U.S. publication model is jurisdiction-specific; a signed edition still requires its amendment/effective-time context and a source-qualified legal applicability decision.

sources.title: Idempotent requests
sources.supported_claim: Stripe documents request-key replay that returns the stored first result, checks parameter equality, and may prune keys after at least 24 hours; concurrent requests and pre-execution validation failures have separate behavior.
sources.limits: This is a vendor-specific bounded idempotency window, not exactly-once execution or a universal provider contract. Once the key expires, a replay may execute again.

sources.title: Cryptographic attestation - AWS Nitro Enclaves
sources.supported_claim: Nitro uses signed attestation documents with enclave measurements that an external service or AWS KMS can check before authorizing selected operations. AWS documents that enclaves have isolated memory/vCPUs, no persistent storage or direct external network connectivity, and communicate through the parent instance's vsock path.
sources.limits: This proves a bounded execution identity under the provider's model, not legal permission, correct result semantics, upstream raw-source truth, every external log/temp sink, or post-run deletion. Third-party verifiers need their own policy and validation.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.supported_claim: PROV-O represents entities, activities, agents, derivation, invalidation and qualified roles, and allows application-specific specialization.
sources.limits: It records provenance structure; it does not establish relation truth, method validity, independence or admissibility.

sources.title: Logical Decoding Concepts, PostgreSQL 18
sources.supported_claim: A logical slot can pair an exported snapshot with a later ordered change stream; changes may replay after crash, consumers must handle duplicates, and slots retain WAL/catalog resources.
sources.limits: Specific to PostgreSQL and its log scope; does not include external claim, rights or publisher stores.

sources.title: Transaction Isolation, PostgreSQL 18
sources.supported_claim: Serializable excludes transaction serialization anomalies; weaker Read Committed reads can see distinct snapshots across commands.
sources.limits: Isolation covers only one database transaction.

sources.title: Transactional outbox pattern, AWS Prescriptive Guidance
sources.supported_claim: A local outbox transaction closes the database/event dual-write gap; relays may duplicate, so consumers must be idempotent and preserve needed order.
sources.limits: Does not atomically commit downstream services or external effects.

sources.title: Saga orchestration pattern, AWS Prescriptive Guidance
sources.supported_claim: Cross-store workflows use local transactions, forward recovery or compensation; participants need idempotency and the pattern is eventually consistent without isolation.
sources.limits: Compensation is another act, not guaranteed rollback or global atomic commit.

sources.title: Exactly-once source connectors, Apache Kafka Connect 4.2
sources.supported_claim: Exactly-once source support requires meaningful source offsets and exact resume without loss or duplication; task generations can be fenced within Kafka Connect.
sources.limits: Not a transaction across arbitrary external sources, claim ledger, CAS, rights and publisher.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.supported_claim: If-Match uses strong entity-tag comparison to prevent stale state-changing updates; If-Range resumes only on an exact strong validator match.
sources.limits: A validator is an origin assertion, not independent completeness or byte-integrity evidence.

sources.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
sources.supported_claim: 304 updates and reuses a suitable stored response selected by URI, request variant and validators.
sources.limits: 304 has no replacement body; without the exact stored representation it cannot reconstruct a complete capture.

sources.title: Conditional writes, Amazon S3
sources.supported_claim: If-Match conditional writes fail when current ETag differs; concurrent writes/deletes can produce precondition, conflict or not-found outcomes.
sources.limits: Protects one S3 object update, not another database head or semantic currentness.

sources.title: Object API: ETag, Amazon S3
sources.supported_claim: ETag is not necessarily a full-object MD5 for multipart uploads or some encryption modes.
sources.limits: Conditional-write validator and independently computed content digest are different evidence.

sources.title: Detecting Activity failures, Temporal
sources.supported_claim: Retries create another attempt; heartbeat payload can resume progress and cancellation is delivered through heartbeat processing.
sources.limits: Timeout/cancellation does not prove a provider-side operation stopped.

sources.title: Idempotent requests, Stripe API
sources.supported_claim: Stripe API v1 saves first response after execution begins, compares request parameters, and may prune keys after at least 24 hours; reuse after pruning starts a new call.
sources.limits: Provider- and API-version-specific; does not prove a remote effect after lost reply.

sources.title: Retaining multiple versions of objects with S3 Versioning
sources.supported_claim: Normal delete inserts a current marker and leaves older versions retrievable; permanent removal requires version-specific delete and lifecycle handling.
sources.limits: Shows one S3 bucket behavior, not PolicyOS or every store.

sources.title: Locking objects with Object Lock, Amazon S3
sources.supported_claim: Retention/legal hold applies to specified object versions; compliance mode can prevent deletion during retention and governance mode has authorized bypass.
sources.limits: Storage control is not a legal applicability decision or complete copy inventory.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Articles 17 and 89
sources.supported_claim: Erasure is tied to specified grounds and exceptions include legal obligation and qualifying public-interest archiving/research with Article 89 safeguards; Article 17(2) addresses reasonable steps to inform other controllers.
sources.limits: Applicability depends on facts, role, jurisdiction and other law; PolicyOS consumes the competent decision.

sources.title: Handling Overload, Site Reliability Engineering
sources.supported_claim: Request counts and static request attributes can be poor capacity proxies because work costs differ and change. The source recommends graceful degradation and transparent errors under overload, and describes isolating batch load from higher-priority traffic.
sources.limits: A serving-system design discussion, not a PolicyOS resource contract or evidence that any local resource is currently measured or enforced.

sources.title: Dominant Resource Fairness: Fair Allocation of Multiple Resource Types
sources.supported_claim: Dominant Resource Fairness generalizes max-min fairness to heterogeneous multi-resource demands and studies properties including strategy-proofness and envy-freeness under its model.
sources.limits: Fair allocation is not a normative rule for custody duties, urgency, protected actions, or legal priority. The paper does not implement reservations, terminal fan-in, or PolicyOS process accounting.

sources.title: Control Group v2, Linux Kernel Documentation
sources.supported_claim: cgroup v2 provides hierarchical CPU, memory, and I/O controls and accounting. Its documentation distinguishes weights, protections, and limits; memory.high throttles under reclaim while memory.max can invoke the OOM killer and may be exceeded temporarily.
sources.limits: Only applies where the host, kernel, filesystem, controller, and process placement support the relevant controls. It does not meter every network/provider spend or supply a product-level reserve protocol.

sources.title: Memory Management in DuckDB
sources.supported_claim: DuckDB's documented memory_limit only applies to its buffer manager, and its temporary-directory limit is configurable (the documented default is unlimited). This shows why an engine-specific memory setting is not a whole-process or disk cap.
sources.limits: DuckDB documents limits for its own operators. It is not a governed PolicyOS spill destination or a universal bound on native/process memory.

sources.title: Memory Management in DuckDB
sources.supported_claim: DuckDB can stream and spill larger-than-memory intermediates to a temporary directory. If memory is exceeded and spilling is disabled, the temporary-directory limit is exceeded, or spilling is unavailable for a query, DuckDB reports an out-of-memory error and cancels the query.
sources.limits: DuckDB documents behavior for its own operators. It does not establish a governed PolicyOS spill destination, retention/right scope, or whole-process memory bound.

sources.title: Skyframe, Bazel Reference
sources.supported_claim: Incremental recomputation depends on functions declaring all inputs through the dependency graph; Bazel describes reverse-transitive invalidation and change pruning after recomputation.
sources.limits: Build-system dependencies do not encode PolicyOS rights, semantic validity, audiences, authority, or scientific independence. Unregistered reads defeat the incremental correctness model.

sources.title: dvc.yaml Files and dvc.lock, DVC Documentation
sources.supported_claim: DVC lockfiles record stage definitions, dependencies, parameters, and output hashes so the pipeline can detect changed stages and decide which stages to reproduce.
sources.limits: A reproducible pipeline cache does not decide current legal use or whether a derivative is admissible for a particular audience and purpose.

sources.title: Apache Avro Specification
sources.supported_claim: Avro requires a writer schema to interpret encoded data and defines reader/writer schema resolution, including field matching and default behavior.
sources.limits: Structural schema resolution cannot prove that a field retained the same substantive meaning or is sufficient for a selected consumer.

sources.title: Schema Evolution and Compatibility for Schema Registry
sources.supported_claim: Backward, forward, full, and transitive compatibility answer different old/new reader questions; transitive checks cover more than the latest prior version, and compatibility choices constrain producer/consumer rollout order.
sources.limits: These compatibility checks are schema-format specific and do not establish semantic equivalence, rights, or source-cut consistency.

sources.title: The Update Framework Specification v1.0.33
sources.supported_claim: TUF separates trust roles and uses versioned, expiring metadata and snapshots to address rollback, freeze, and mix-and-match attacks in software update repositories.
sources.limits: TUF is a software-update trust framework; it cannot bootstrap PolicyOS institutional authority, settle source rights, or certify semantic compatibility.

sources.title: Language Guide (proto3), Protocol Buffers
sources.supported_claim: Proto3 preserves unknown fields in binary messages in common round trips, while converting through JSON or rebuilding messages field-by-field can lose them; parseability alone does not protect unknown data through every transformation.
sources.limits: Wire-format compatibility is not a consumer-requiredness or semantic adequacy decision.

sources.title: Stateful Stream Processing, Apache Flink Documentation
sources.supported_claim: Flink checkpoints bind positions in input streams to corresponding operator state; recovery restores the latest completed checkpoint and replays sources from those positions. Exactly-once state consistency depends on replayable sources, and unaligned checkpoints trade lower barrier delay for persisted in-flight data and extra I/O.
sources.limits: This is a coordinated stream-processing snapshot, not evidence that independently sampled PolicyOS sources share a global cut or that a policy claim is true.

sources.title: SLSA Build Provenance v1.2
sources.supported_claim: SLSA provenance defines verifiable build information, including the subject, builder identity, build type, invocation parameters, resolved dependencies, metadata, and useful byproducts.
sources.limits: Build provenance traces how an artifact was built; it does not establish semantic acceptance, complete consumer coverage, independent scientific evidence, or PolicyOS authority.

sources.title: Certified Kubernetes Software Conformance, CNCF
sources.supported_claim: The Kubernetes conformance program runs an identical open-source test application, submits results for review, and lets end users rerun that application to check interoperability against required APIs.
sources.limits: The tested Kubernetes API profile and certification do not generalize to PolicyOS semantics; the useful transfer is an exact version/profile-scoped test corpus plus review and rerun identity.

sources.title: MLIR Language Reference
sources.supported_claim: Multiple dialects can coexist in a module, an analogy for typed stages over common IR.
sources.limits: Compiler analogy only; not policy semantics or reason to adopt MLIR.

sources.title: Dialect Conversion - MLIR
sources.supported_claim: Conversion declares legal/illegal operations and explicit rewrite patterns, optionally type conversion.
sources.limits: Structural translation does not verify meaning or authority.

sources.title: Pass Infrastructure - MLIR
sources.supported_claim: Passes declare dialect dependencies and explicit transformation stages.
sources.limits: No local performance or adoption case.

sources.title: CP-SAT Solver
sources.supported_claim: Integer constraints and distinct OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, MODEL_INVALID and UNKNOWN statuses; UNKNOWN can mean incomplete/resource limited.
sources.limits: Only encoded constraint search, not facts, causal validity or admissibility.

sources.title: Programming Z3
sources.supported_claim: SAT/model queries, incremental scopes and tracked assumptions; unsat cores need not be minimal.
sources.limits: Encoded formulas only; cannot validate source truth or grant authority.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.supported_claim: Vocabulary for provenance entities, activities, agents and relations.
sources.limits: Lineage is not truth, independence, admissibility or authority.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.supported_claim: Validates RDF graphs against declared shapes and emits reports.
sources.limits: Shape conformance is not real-world truth or institutional act.

sources.title: Safe Policy Improvement with Baseline Bootstrapping
sources.supported_claim: Bounds candidate changes and falls back to baseline for uncertain state-action regions under stated MDP/data assumptions.
sources.limits: Guarantees do not transfer to public policy justification or permission.

sources.title: Policy Language | Open Policy Agent
sources.supported_claim: Rego declaratively evaluates policy over structured data.
sources.limits: Rule evaluation does not supply causal grounds, evidence custody or admissibility.

sources.title: Towards Causal Model-Based Policy Optimization
sources.supported_claim: Studies SCM intervention simulation in policy optimization and spurious predictive correlations under shift.
sources.limits: Preprint/RL results do not prove local capacity, institutional safety or acceptance.

sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
sources.supported_claim: Adaptive reuse of a holdout can overfit to that holdout; their reusable-holdout construction controls this through a restricted validation interface and privacy/stability arguments.
sources.limits: This does not make a sealed file or checksum a privacy mechanism. PolicyOS has no adopted query budget or privacy guarantee here, so use this as the reason to protect AS2 and reject post-hoc tuning, not as a transferred guarantee.

sources.title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
sources.supported_claim: Confidence sequences can give time-uniform coverage over an unbounded horizon under their stated stochastic conditions, including validity at arbitrary stopping times.
sources.limits: A sequential interval does not cure holdout leakage, post-hoc outcome selection, cause misclassification, or context transport. GYD-08 asks for repeated-look failure fixtures, not adoption of a new sequential guarantee.

sources.title: SAFFRON: an Adaptive Algorithm for Online Control of the False Discovery Rate
sources.supported_claim: Online FDR procedures require valid sequential p-values; SAFFRON states conditional super-uniformity assumptions and derives its guarantees from them.
sources.limits: It is a method comparison, not the local controller's theorem and not evidence that PolicyOS DDM outputs satisfy its assumptions.

sources.title: The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency
sources.supported_claim: Benjamini-Yekutieli prove FDR control for the linear step-up procedure under positive regression dependence on true-null test statistics.
sources.limits: That condition is not arbitrary dependence, and the result is an offline multiple-testing result rather than an online DDM-stream guarantee.

sources.title: Online multiple testing with e-values
sources.supported_claim: The paper's e-LOND procedure gives online FDR control under arbitrary, possibly unknown, dependence when its input e-values meet the e-value validity conditions.
sources.limits: An anomaly score or current p-value is not an e-value by naming. This is a future alternative only if the accepted DDM plan and native producers supply the required evidence; it is not a default replacement.

sources.title: Transportability of Causal and Statistical Relations: A Formal Approach
sources.supported_claim: Selection diagrams make differences and commonalities between source and target environments explicit and support deciding whether a causal effect is identifiable in the target from available source experiments and target observations.
sources.limits: This does not license automatic generalization to a new population, time, or interference regime. It depends on a causal graph and evidence for its selection assumptions.

sources.title: The Update Framework Specification, version 1.0.36
sources.supported_claim: TUF specifies version, signature, hash, and expiry checks that detect rollback, freeze, and mix-and-match attacks in software update metadata.
sources.limits: TUF is not a causal model-update protocol. Transfer only the narrow design lesson that a consumer resolves a pinned version and rejects stale or mismatched lineage; do not import its signing roles or claim its security properties for Fabric.

sources.title: MLflow Model Registry Workflows
sources.supported_claim: MLflow distinguishes exact model-version references from mutable aliases; alias reassignment can change which version a later consumer resolves.
sources.limits: This is an implementation example, not a recommendation to add MLflow or use aliases for PolicyOS authority. Audit and causal lineage should resolve immutable artifact refs.

sources.title: Adopted reading clarification: competing causal completions and claim-type-specific grounds
sources.supported_claim: A singular world-model reference may be credal/set-valued and admit competing causal completions. Grounding is claim-type-specific: causal claims need causal grounds, measurement claims need construct/method grounds, and value claims need a declared frame and applicable mandate.
sources.limits: This adopted target clarification does not certify implementation or impose a unique causal structure; actual admission still needs the relevant owner, evidence, and scope.

sources.title: Adopted target extension: joint evaluation witness
sources.supported_claim: Whole-design joint evaluation may use simulation or an exact joint derivation/other validated joint witness for the concrete property it actually proves; marginal or pairwise checks do not substitute. Model truth and grounding remain separate.
sources.limits: The alternative needs an explicit property, assumptions, consumer, and falsifier; this target wording does not certify a runtime implementation.

sources.title: Adopted target extension: inference plurality
sources.supported_claim: Bayesian confirmatory updates remain supported, while explicitly justified frequentist, sequential, robust, or partial-identification profiles are also permitted for the propositions they support. Posterior probability, coverage, identification sets, and procedural no-number claims must not be silently mixed.
sources.limits: C02 appoints no method owner, authorizes no posterior mutation, and does not transfer any method guarantee without its own assumptions and bridge.

sources.title: Universal design system Rule 12: corpus discovery and conforming resource growth
sources.supported_claim: Capability is discovered by bounded search over the corpus rather than a hand-maintained central enumeration; a correctly added resource conforming to an existing semantic/protocol class is usable with zero new central code.
sources.limits: A genuinely new transport or semantic capability still needs a typed native extension and conformance; search completeness and capacity remain governed and evidenced.

sources.title: Stage 0 custody kernel K14 scope amendment
sources.supported_claim: Independence is required for verification claims, including benchmark-oracle claims and assertions of independent validation. A same-code rebuild is permitted and establishes consistency, not correctness.
sources.limits: Do not impose a separately owned evaluator on every ordinary rebuild; independence remains necessary when the claimed property or explicit verification claim requires it.

sources.title: GY engine subordination plan, §9 Phase 7 verification criteria
sources.supported_claim: The original V1–V7 criteria, including V4 negatives a–v, define the evidence this proposal must preserve.
sources.limits: Historical planning source; its implementation and product verification status remain planned_after_E02_acceptance and UNRUN in the assigned input. Rebind to the accepted E02 source before execution.

sources.title: R9/GY/Atlas workstream 03, GY tasks
sources.supported_claim: The workstream preserves task timing, formal status conflicts, final freeze/replay ordering, shared artifacts and no-duplicate-wave requirements.
sources.limits: Planning evidence only; it cannot establish a product result or accepted tree.

sources.title: Execution 07 scoped readiness and edge decisions
sources.supported_claim: Accepted-source rebind must resolve exact source, affected consumers, schemas/rules and relevant semantic fields; interface agreement is planning only.
sources.limits: Does not turn verification preparation into a global completion barrier or substitute for the named final execution receipt.

sources.title: GY capability coverage matrix checker
sources.supported_claim: A native matrix checker exists and can be extended at its current ownership boundary.
sources.limits: At the historical observation it validates declared matrix content and derived summaries; it does not itself establish the complete moved-row denominator or that each declared capability is behaviorally present and consumed.

sources.title: Workspace production loop and production-trigger proof owner
sources.supported_claim: The canonical WorkspaceLoop has a real-CAS production-case path and distinguishes production evidence from fixture execution; the historical implementation describes its refusal-path limits.
sources.limits: Source inspection and a route-shaped ProductionLoopRunProof do not prove an actual measurement-rooted outcome, persisted artifacts, or consumer readback.

sources.title: Research DAG replay owner
sources.supported_claim: The current owner can reconstruct a persisted high-level agentic decision/provenance trace without making new live calls.
sources.limits: Trace reconstruction is not deterministic provider re-execution, byte-identical output replay, or promoted-artifact revalidation.

sources.title: GY evidence canonical hash helper
sources.supported_claim: A native canonical evidence hash helper exists and removes selected volatile values before hashing.
sources.limits: At the historical observation it also strips keys ending in _at and _duration; this is not safe evidence that authority-relevant effective/as-of/source times are preserved in the digest.

sources.title: Health metric governance owner (G8)
sources.supported_claim: One existing owner normalizes health metric aliases, captures source snapshots, emits trend/cross-metric diagnoses, and distinguishes domain from search ceiling with anti-gaming checks; Cycle Board is an existing surface.
sources.limits: This is a diagnostic metric governance owner, not causal identification or authority for useful-design-rate optimization.

sources.title: Policy Design Case failure/repair register
sources.supported_claim: P29–P41 require behavioral proof, resolve/content-bind/verifier provenance, adversarial variants, completed exclusion isolation, complete denominators, gate predicate provenance/property divergence, companion-aware budgeting, and correct-base red replay.
sources.limits: Pattern guidance constrains honest evidence and implementation shape; it does not itself prove any V1–V7 product property.

sources.title: Hypothesis Quickstart
sources.supported_claim: Property-based examples can be generated through ordinary Python test functions and run by pytest/unittest; example volume is configurable.
sources.limits: Generated examples explore the supplied strategy and property; they do not establish oracle correctness, source-set completeness, or proof over all inputs.

sources.title: Hypothesis stateful testing
sources.supported_claim: Rule-based stateful tests generate action sequences, can compare an implementation with a reference model, and shrink failures to shorter sequences.
sources.limits: The reference model and action language can omit the very transition that matters; sequence generation is not evidence that the model covers PolicyOS lifecycle semantics.

sources.title: Metamorphic Testing: A New Approach for Generating Next Test Cases (HKUST-CS98-01)
sources.supported_claim: Metamorphic testing derives follow-up test cases and expected relations from successful cases when a direct oracle is difficult to obtain.
sources.limits: The chosen relation is itself a premise; relations must be reasoned from the original criterion and challenged with adversarial variants, not treated as self-validating.

sources.title: Toward Just-in-time and Language-agnostic Mutation Testing
sources.supported_claim: Mutation testing checks whether tests detect injected faults; full campaigns can be expensive, motivating focused and incremental mutants.
sources.limits: A surviving or killed mutant speaks only to that mutation and test oracle; a small targeted set does not estimate all defect coverage.

sources.title: Open Containers Initiative Image Specification: Descriptor
sources.supported_claim: A content consumer should verify referenced bytes against the descriptor digest and size.
sources.limits: A digest binds bytes; by itself it does not establish semantic validity, correct provenance, a runtime environment, or authority.

sources.title: PyTorch reproducibility notes
sources.supported_claim: Reproducibility is scoped to software/hardware conditions; deterministic choices may be slower or unavailable, and cross-release/platform bit identity is not a general promise.
sources.limits: This documents PyTorch-specific behavior, not the PolicyOS runtime; use it to scope replay claims, not as evidence that local operations are nondeterministic or slow.

sources.title: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH reproducible-builds documentation
sources.supported_claim: Normalizing build timestamps can remove one source of build variation.
sources.limits: Controlling one timestamp does not establish whole-program, model, data, hardware, or semantic reproducibility.

sources.title: Estimating Causal Effects of Treatments in Randomized and Nonrandomized Studies
sources.supported_claim: Causal effect estimation requires controlled comparisons and explicit assumptions; randomization is useful where possible, with careful nonrandomized designs sometimes necessary.
sources.limits: A descriptive health-signal dashboard or cross-metric association is not itself an identified causal effect.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions for OFR
sources.supported_claim: NARA says each Federal Register issue and its published documents are permanent records; a published document cannot be altered or unpublished, and a correction, withdrawal or rescission requires the issuing agency to publish a new document.
sources.limits: This is a US federal legal-record rule, not a PolicyOS authority grant. Transfer only the append-and-link history pattern; external institutions retain their own decision authority.

sources.title: New govinfo API
sources.supported_claim: GovInfo describes unique package and granule identifiers, multiple content renditions, descriptive MODS metadata, and preservation PREMIS metadata including fixity. Its official record example separates an issue package from individual document granules.
sources.limits: GovInfo's package model is an example, not a requirement to add a PolicyOS package database or adopt its IDs. Preserve the local exact ArtifactRef and selected manifest view.

sources.title: Federal Register collection help
sources.supported_claim: GovInfo distinguishes the official published Federal Register from its earlier public-inspection material and explains that a granule ID identifies one document inside an issue; it also has an explicit corrections section.
sources.limits: The legal timing and status are specific to the Federal Register. Do not transfer its legal effects, and do not treat FederalRegister.gov's explicitly unofficial XML display as the authoritative record.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.supported_claim: WCAG 2.2 defines testable, technology-independent criteria. Relevant examples include text resize, reflow without loss at 320 CSS px, programmatic status messages, keyboard focus visibility/order, and name/role/value.
sources.limits: WCAG conformance is scoped to the tested pages and criteria and does not establish human comprehension or an audience's understanding of policy meaning.

sources.title: Guidance to meet the Plain Language standard
sources.supported_claim: DfE distinguishes generic plain-English techniques from plain language adapted to user needs and user-research findings; technical terms can be retained where needed but should be explained.
sources.limits: This is UK public-service guidance. It supports audience-qualified review as a method but does not establish the required PolicyOS audiences, locales, or wording.

sources.title: Understand content design
sources.supported_claim: GOV.UK content design starts from user needs, considers the best format and place to publish, calls for clear accessible plain-English content, and distinguishes current content from historical content retained as a record.
sources.limits: This is content guidance, not an archival retention standard and not a decision on PolicyOS Trust/Docs ownership.

sources.title: Communicating quality, uncertainty and change
sources.supported_claim: The GSS guidance recommends explaining source quality, uncertainty, limitations, context, and intended use so that readers can judge fit for use; it warns that excess certainty can prompt unsupported conclusions.
sources.limits: The page is from 2018, currently marked under review, and says it has not incorporated accessibility legislation. It concerns statistics, so use only as a communication example, not as a PolicyOS rule or legal standard.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.supported_claim: PROV-O supplies interoperable Entity, Activity, and Agent provenance terms and relations for use, generation, attribution, derivation, and responsibility.
sources.limits: A provenance vocabulary cannot prove lawful use, correct interpretation, source independence, institutional mandate, or PolicyOS admissibility.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.supported_claim: DCAT 3 distinguishes a resource's versions and previous-version chain, dataset series, and distributions such as different language or format representations; it also models issued and modified dates separately.
sources.limits: DCAT is a dataset-catalog vocabulary. Its concepts may inform typed projections and links, but it is not a PolicyOS record schema or status/authority calculus.

sources.title: Visualizing Uncertainty in Sets (IEEE VIS 2024 / IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications)
sources.source_kind: original research article and official IEEE VIS paper page
sources.supported_claim: The paper separates uncertainty affecting set membership, set attributes, and element attributes, and distinguishes certainty, undefined uncertainty, and quantifiable uncertainty. This supports separate display treatment for known sets, uncertain membership, and quantified value.
sources.limits: A conceptual framework and examples, not an evaluation of PolicyOS or an admissibility rule.

sources.title: Approximation and Visualization of Pareto Frontier in the Framework of Classical Approach to Multi-Objective Optimization
sources.source_kind: original research paper, Dagstuhl Seminar Proceedings
sources.supported_claim: Interactive Decision Maps supports examining a Pareto frontier under conflicting criteria and communicating results in design-variable and objective spaces. This is a precedent for showing a frontier when criteria do not license a single rank.
sources.limits: The paper addresses optimization; it does not define PolicyOS value semantics or authorize scalar aggregation.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification 3.1.1
sources.supported_claim: Schema Objects use JSON Schema; oneOf validates exactly one listed alternative. A discriminator is a selection hint and must not change validation, and alternatives must be listed explicitly beside oneOf.
sources.limits: The specification does not guarantee a configured generator emits a correct client union or that clients validate hostile runtime payloads.

sources.title: OpenAPI Generator supported generators
sources.supported_claim: The project offers multiple client generators, including TypeScript targets, so the generated client family can remain the API-to-client bridge.
sources.limits: Availability does not prove oneOf fidelity for this repository's selected generator/version; actual generated output and consumer need verification.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.supported_claim: The model distinguishes entities, activities, usage, generation, derivation, attribution, time, and invalidation; these relations help describe exact lineage and lifecycle.
sources.limits: PROV does not verify a producer, establish currentness or lawful use, or confer authority.

sources.title: TypeScript Handbook: Narrowing and exhaustiveness
sources.supported_claim: Literal discriminants narrow union members; never-based exhaustiveness makes a new variant fail compilation in an unhandled switch.
sources.limits: Static exhaustiveness does not validate untrusted JSON at runtime or replace an API schema.

sources.title: TypeScript Handbook: Classes
sources.supported_claim: TypeScript private modifiers are erased and provide design-time checks; ECMAScript private fields, closures, and WeakMaps provide runtime privacy mechanisms.
sources.limits: Runtime privacy does not authenticate a network payload or appoint an institution.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Transaction Isolation
sources.supported_claim: At Read Committed, a concurrent updater waits and re-evaluates the WHERE predicate on the committed row; Serializable provides serial execution for committed transactions but applications must handle retries after serialization failures.
sources.limits: Docs do not prove DS20 wiring. Pin the deployed PostgreSQL major, schema, isolation level, transaction boundary, and app behavior.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: Explicit Locking
sources.supported_claim: Row-level FOR UPDATE locks block conflicting writers and lockers until transaction end.
sources.limits: A lock does not cover mutation or persistence after its transaction ends or in another store.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: INSERT
sources.supported_claim: A unique conflict target and ON CONFLICT provide an atomic insert/update result under concurrency; RETURNING reports rows actually affected. A unique single-use token row can support one-winner replay handling.
sources.limits: The SQL primitive does not prove the application uses it at the correct boundary or maps a loser to the required response.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18: UPDATE
sources.supported_claim: UPDATE supports a conditional WHERE predicate and RETURNING values for rows actually updated, exposing whether an expected-revision comparison matched.
sources.limits: A SQL example is not a Fabric capability receipt; a post-check or later mutation is outside its atomic boundary.

sources.title: Helm Provenance and Integrity
sources.supported_claim: Helm package provenance binds a chart package checksum to a signature, and helm install --verify aborts when verification fails.
sources.limits: A valid signature does not prove an embedded policy mirror equals the canonical source policy set. The current page warns that it is not fully updated for Helm 4; only generic package checksum/signature integrity is relied on. Rebind command behavior to the actually deployed major before execution.

sources.title: The Value of Information and Stochastic Programming
sources.supported_claim: Expected value of perfect information is an expected gain in the decision objective and an upper bound on what is worth spending to acquire the information.
sources.limits: This perfect-information bound is not a numeric VOI producer for DS15's finite route or a cost schedule.

sources.title: On the Value of Information Across Decision Problems
sources.supported_claim: Expected utility increase and buying price are distinct value-of-information measures and need not rank information sources identically across decision problems.
sources.limits: The paper does not supply PolicyOS's missing utility, route, cost basis, or numeric producer.

sources.title: DSL Migration
sources.source_kind: first-party software architecture article by the pattern author
sources.supported_claim: Versioned DSL change can use small incremental migration programs or version-specific parsers and a semantic model; migrations should preserve information important to authors.
sources.limits: Practitioner guidance, not a PolicyOS schema decision; the native owner chooses the semantics.

sources.title: Parallel Change
sources.source_kind: first-party software architecture article by the pattern author
sources.supported_claim: Expand/migrate/contract lets clients move incrementally before the old interface is removed; temporary dual support has coordination cost and needs a real completion point.
sources.limits: The pattern does not justify permanently maintaining duplicate semantics or auto-upgrading historical authority.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) Version 3
sources.supported_claim: DCAT 3 distinguishes cataloged datasets, distributions, data services and dataset series; it adds version/current-version relations and supports multiple representations and temporal/spatial metadata.
sources.limits: A catalog vocabulary supports interoperability and discovery. It does not establish that content is authentic, lawful to reuse, applicable, current for a claim, or authoritative.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.supported_claim: PROV-O provides reusable relations among entities, activities and agents, including generation, use, derivation and attribution, for expressing lineage.
sources.limits: A lineage graph records declared provenance. It does not prove independence, factual truth, legal permission, or source quality unless those properties have their own evidence and verification.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.supported_claim: SHACL validates an RDF data graph against a versioned shapes graph and can emit a validation report.
sources.limits: SHACL is a possible validation format when an owner already uses RDF. Structural conformance alone is not semantic adequacy or authority, and adopting it would not justify a second registry.

sources.title: OECD SDMX API
sources.supported_claim: The OECD documents separate data queries from structure queries and identifies agency, dataset and dataset version as components of a data query.
sources.limits: API structure and version paths help bind a query and representation. They do not prove completeness, fitness for a local estimand, or stable availability.

sources.title: OECD API best practices and recommendations
sources.supported_claim: The OECD recommends its content-constraint query as a way to read a dataset ValidFrom time and observation count and check whether a dataset version changed.
sources.limits: A change detector is a trigger for refresh and revalidation, not an integrity, currentness, or applicability verdict.

sources.title: World Bank Indicators API basic call structures
sources.supported_claim: The API documents date and source parameters, language variants, page and per_page controls, and returns pagination metadata such as page count and total records.
sources.limits: The endpoint requires complete paging and exact parameter capture where paging is used. The API describes an aggregate indicator service, not a selected case source or household-level dataset.

sources.title: Consolidated texts
sources.supported_claim: EUR-Lex states that consolidated texts show rules applicable at a point in time but have no legal effect; its page identifies the amendments included in a consolidation.
sources.limits: This is an EU publisher's rule about its consolidations, not a universal rule for other jurisdictions. The exact governing legal source and effectivity rules remain case-specific.

sources.title: European Legislation Identifier
sources.supported_claim: ELI provides web identifiers and metadata for legislation, including point-in-time versions and language/format distinctions in its URI model.
sources.limits: An identifier resolves a resource or version; it does not determine legal effect, notice, competence, applicability, or the authoritative language for another jurisdiction.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0 XML Vocabulary
sources.supported_claim: Akoma Ntoso describes legal document lifecycle events and links those events to the individual documents that produced them; it distinguishes original, single and multiple versions.
sources.limits: A document format can preserve and link legal material but cannot make a legal interpretation or establish the competence of the issuer.

sources.title: OECD Income Distribution Database metadata
sources.supported_claim: OECD documents its equivalised disposable household income definition, its treatment of income components and persons as the distribution unit, and notes the square-root household scale is a common but arbitrary choice.
sources.limits: The documented OECD convention explains that dataset's construction; it does not establish that the same construct or scale fits a different population or policy question.

sources.title: OECD Income Distribution Database guidelines
sources.supported_claim: The guidelines distinguish household survey observation units from person-level distribution indicators, weight households by member count, and prescribe an equivalence elasticity of 0.5 for that series.
sources.limits: The prescribed definition harmonizes the OECD series; a shared label does not guarantee local frame, accounting, equivalisation, or period comparability.

sources.title: On the measurement of inequality
sources.source_kind: Original research paper, author work hosted by a university
sources.supported_claim: Atkinson derives inequality measurement from an explicit social-welfare approach and contrasts ranking distributions with quantifying inequality, illustrating that a measure embeds choices about distributional sensitivity.
sources.limits: This paper supplies a method and assumptions, not authorization to select an inequality-aversion parameter for a case.

sources.title: Counting and multidimensional poverty measurement
sources.supported_claim: Alkire and Foster describe within-dimension deprivation cutoffs, a cross-dimension cutoff, and an adjusted headcount measure that captures incidence and breadth.
sources.limits: Dimension weights and cutoffs are substantive choices; the paper does not make them universally correct or supply local authorization.

sources.title: Causal Inference: What If
sources.source_kind: Methods book by original researchers, versioned living publication
sources.supported_claim: Hernán and Robins frame observational causal analysis as emulation of a specified target trial and discuss exchangeability, positivity, consistency, treatment versions and longitudinal methods.
sources.limits: The site points to a revisable edition; a use must pin the exact version. Its methods do not choose a policy objective or certify a case's assumptions.

sources.title: External Validity: From Do-Calculus to Transportability Across Populations
sources.supported_claim: Pearl and Bareinboim use selection diagrams to represent differences between study and target populations and derive conditions under which causal effects can be transported.
sources.limits: The diagram's assumptions require substantive support. Formal transportability does not rescue absent overlap or an ungrounded account of population differences.

sources.title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics
sources.supported_claim: Van Calster and colleagues distinguish calibration assessment from other predictive-model performance and describe calibration checks for external validation.
sources.limits: Predictive calibration on a target sample is neither causal identification nor proof that the target sample represents a policy population.

sources.title: Good practice principles for deliberative processes for public decision making
sources.supported_claim: OECD's principles include a clear remit, accountability, transparency, representativeness, inclusion, accessible information, deliberation, adequate time, independence, privacy and evaluation.
sources.limits: These are process design principles drawn from comparative practice, not a legal mandate, universal representation test, or substitute for the commissioning authority's decision.

sources.title: OECD Guidelines for Citizen Participation Processes
sources.supported_claim: The guidelines distinguish participation methods and policy-cycle stages, and recommend stating expected outcomes and how citizen input will be used or answered.
sources.limits: Participation can inform issue framing, formulation, decision, implementation or evaluation, but a participation record alone does not establish an authorized decision.

sources.title: The Green Book (2026)
sources.supported_claim: The guidance says it does not set objectives or make policy decisions and requires weighted distributional estimates to appear alongside unweighted estimates.
sources.limits: Its weights and procedures are UK-specific policy guidance, not universal defaults. It is useful here as an example of explicitly exposing value choices and preserving the decision maker's role.

sources.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
sources.source_kind: Original practice paper in Data Science Journal
sources.supported_claim: The paper articulates collective benefit, authority to control, responsibility and ethics as people- and purpose-oriented considerations in Indigenous data governance.
sources.limits: Apply only where the relevant peoples, communities and their governing authorities make these principles relevant; it is not a generic permission token or replacement for local rights.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook, Chapter 4: Searching for and selecting studies
sources.supported_claim: Cochrane recommends searches matched to eligibility criteria, broad source coverage, reproducible exact search strategies and record counts, and distinguishes reports from underlying studies.
sources.limits: Search recommendations arise from health evidence synthesis and need adaptation to other fields, languages, source types and lawful access constraints.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook, Chapter 22: Prospective approaches to accumulating evidence
sources.supported_claim: Cochrane's living-review guidance calls for explicit search methods and update frequency, ongoing surveillance, and communication of what changed between versions.
sources.limits: The handbook does not prescribe a universal refresh interval; use depends on source change rates, decision stakes and resource constraints.

sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.supported_claim: Benjamini and Hochberg introduce a step-up procedure that controls false discovery rate under independent test statistics.
sources.limits: Independence conditions and the tested family matter; this is not a blanket license to promote adaptive findings or use the procedure without checking dependence assumptions.

sources.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
sources.supported_claim: The paper shows that repeated adaptive reuse of a holdout can overfit it and presents a method for controlling that risk.
sources.limits: The method's guarantees depend on its formal setting and algorithm. It is a warning and possible design family, not evidence that PolicyOS has independent validation.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.supported_claim: SQLite WAL permits readers alongside a writer but requires all database processes on one host, does not work over a network filesystem, and the WAL file is part of persistent state.
sources.limits: SQLite storage behavior does not establish the durability or locking semantics of an untested filesystem/container volume.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.supported_claim: The Online Backup API can copy a live database as a snapshot while allowing writes between brief source reads; raw file copying has failure and locking limitations.
sources.limits: A database snapshot alone does not capture CAS objects, source rights, revocations, credentials, or provider-side effects.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Backup and Restore
sources.supported_claim: PostgreSQL presents SQL dump, filesystem backup, and continuous archiving as distinct methods with different assumptions; PITR depends on a base backup and a suitable WAL archive.
sources.limits: The current docs do not select a PolicyOS RPO/RTO or prove the selected operator's backup chain.

sources.title: systemd.service
sources.supported_claim: systemd supports restart-on-failure for long-running services, and automatic restart is subject to start-rate limits.
sources.limits: Process supervision does not provide durable job leases, exactly-once effects, or cross-store transaction semantics.

sources.title: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
sources.supported_claim: Kubernetes distinguishes liveness from readiness; readiness can remove a temporarily unable pod from service without restarting it.
sources.limits: This is a Kubernetes implementation of a useful distinction, not a requirement to deploy Kubernetes.

sources.title: OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization
sources.supported_claim: Every endpoint that accepts an object ID and acts on it needs object-level authorization; identifier unpredictability does not replace that check.
sources.limits: OWASP guidance identifies the class and mitigation, not whether the historical PolicyOS job route is vulnerable.

sources.title: Project runner registration token security update
sources.supported_claim: GitLab reported that a project runner-registration-token vulnerability could expose project-scoped tokens to unauthorized users and reset tokens as mitigation.
sources.limits: This incident supports narrow credential scope and revocation readiness; it is not evidence of a PolicyOS defect.

sources.title: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supported_claim: Secrets should have least-privilege access, lifecycle and audit metadata, expiration/revocation, and short-lived credentials where practicable.
sources.limits: It does not prescribe a single secret manager or eliminate the need for an institution-owned root credential and source-use grant.

sources.title: Idempotent requests
sources.supported_claim: Stripe supports request idempotency keys for safely retrying supported operations, with provider-specific parameter matching and key retention behavior.
sources.limits: Idempotency behavior differs by provider and endpoint; a timeout or this example does not prove another provider did not execute or charge.

sources.title: Control Group v2
sources.supported_claim: Linux cgroup v2 exposes CPU, memory, process and I/O controls; memory.high throttles/reclaims while memory.max is a hard limit that can invoke OOM handling, and child limits can be overcommitted.
sources.limits: Kernel controls bound OS resources for a configured cgroup; they do not by themselves provide application admission, provider spend limits, scratch quotas, or safe semantic outcomes.

sources.title: Pressure Stall Information
sources.supported_claim: Linux PSI measures CPU, memory and I/O stall time and provides threshold triggers suitable for resource-pressure observation and load shedding.
sources.limits: Pressure measurements are signals for an admission policy, not a universal capacity threshold or hard limit.

sources.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
sources.supported_claim: Kubernetes applies CPU limits through throttling and memory limits through kernel OOM behavior; requests guide scheduling and do not assert application-level/provider budgets.
sources.limits: Kubernetes is one placement/enforcement option; these controls do not establish global job admission or semantic authorization.

sources.title: How to prevent object overwrites with conditional writes
sources.supported_claim: S3 conditional writes can prevent a put from replacing an existing key and can use If-Match preconditions; concurrent multipart/delete cases have distinct 409/412 behavior.
sources.limits: Provider-specific behavior, multipart handling, and authorization still require tests against the selected adapter and configuration.

sources.title: Request preconditions
sources.supported_claim: Cloud Storage generation/metageneration preconditions support conditional mutation and help prevent races; a lost response can leave the client uncertain whether a request applied.
sources.limits: Generation conditions are provider-specific and do not make object storage transactional with the control database.

sources.title: The Update Framework Specification v1.0.37
sources.supported_claim: TUF uses an out-of-band trusted root, threshold signatures, sequential root versions, expiry, persisted root metadata, and an out-of-band recovery path if the root threshold is compromised.
sources.limits: TUF is a protocol pattern, not an institutional appointment, legal grant, or required PolicyOS dependency.

sources.title: CISA Alert AA20-352A: Advanced Persistent Threat Compromise
sources.supported_claim: CISA documented the SolarWinds supply-chain compromise and follow-on identity abuse, including malicious software delivered through the update chain and valid SAML tokens minted after signing-certificate compromise.
sources.limits: This demonstrates that signatures and a trusted update path do not prove benign content or continuing identity integrity; it does not define a PolicyOS threat threshold.

sources.title: fsync(2)
sources.supported_claim: Linux fsync flushes file data/metadata, while durable publication of a directory entry may require fsync of the directory.
sources.limits: Filesystem, mount, device-cache, and network-volume behavior must be qualified on the exact deployment target.

sources.title: Metrics: Cardinality limits
sources.supported_claim: OpenTelemetry metrics SDKs bound the number of tracked attribute combinations (the documented default is 2000); additional measurements are folded into an overflow point, preserving overall totals but dropping the original attribute combination. Queries grouping/filtering by those dropped attributes can undercount.
sources.limits: SDK default and behavior are telemetry implementation details, not PolicyOS audit or admission contracts. Exact per-decision evidence still requires a separately authorized durable receipt.

sources.title: Custom Resources
sources.supported_claim: Kubernetes documentation advises against using Custom Resources as storage for application, end-user, or monitoring data because this couples normal workload operation to the Kubernetes API; CRDs are intended for resources used with Kubernetes API/controller conventions.
sources.limits: This is deployment guidance for Kubernetes and does not rule out a narrowly scoped configuration/control object when the API is already an owned interface. It gives no reason to make Kubernetes a mandatory dependency.

sources.title: PolicyOS identity and custody boundary
sources.supported_claim: The four-way scope test is own when absence makes our published claim false; integrate when external output changes our claim validity; observe when only answerability changes; otherwise out_of_scope. Candidate-band unknowns may be carried as declared limitations; authority-band claims fail closed when required scope is unknown.
sources.limits: This is the ratified PolicyOS rule, not a substitute for content-bound evidence establishing the factual predicate in an individual case.

sources.title: Policy design causal operating system north star
sources.supported_claim: PolicyOS is an epistemic custodian: it consumes others' signatures as typed evidence, signs only claims it can custody, and must keep published justification honest across time and world change.
sources.limits: Product identity guidance; it does not appoint external institutions or define an unratified numeric metric.

sources.title: Coverage.py configuration reference
sources.supported_claim: The measured source universe is affected by configured source/include/omit selectors, and source selection changes what a coverage result says it has measured.
sources.limits: Coverage.py measures execution, not PolicyOS instrument input reads; transfer only the need to disclose scope selectors, not its coverage metric or runner.

sources.title: What's in a build environment?
sources.supported_claim: A reproducibility claim has a declared perimeter including tools, versions, operating-system assumptions, locale, timezone, paths, and relevant environment variables; outputs are comparable only within that stated context.
sources.limits: A project guide, not a universal guarantee that two systems will be reproducible or a mandate to adopt containerization.

sources.title: Locking and syncing
sources.supported_claim: uv lock/sync can check metadata-lock consistency, and exact sync removes packages outside the lock; frozen and locked modes have different verification semantics.
sources.limits: A lockfile pins package resolution, not OS/locale/environmental inputs or generated artifact semantics. Repository-specific setup commands remain controlling.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.1.1
sources.supported_claim: An OpenAPI Description consists of its entry document and all referenced documents; reference resolution, base URIs, and cycles affect the meaning and complete surface.
sources.limits: The specification defines the description format, not a particular repository export pipeline or the desired API policy.

sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme
sources.supported_claim: A canonical JSON representation can make hash/signature inputs repeatable across serializers when data satisfies JCS/I-JSON constraints.
sources.limits: Informational RFC, not an Internet Standards Track specification; its number/string constraints may make it unsuitable for some payloads. Reuse an existing canonical serializer first.

sources.title: PEP 387 – Backwards Compatibility Policy
sources.supported_claim: Python's compatibility guidance distinguishes documented public API from merely importable modules and provides a deprecation approach for actual public interfaces.
sources.limits: An ecosystem analogy only. PolicyOS architecture/public_surface/contract.toml and its inventory-review rules control this repository.

sources.title: Pydantic strict mode and models
sources.supported_claim: Strict mode reduces implicit coercion, while Pydantic model validation establishes output types and constraints rather than proving truth of input claims.
sources.limits: Strictness is a parsing boundary only. It is not evidence provenance, authority, or semantic adequacy.

sources.title: Understanding JSON Schema: object properties
sources.supported_claim: JSON Schema permits additional properties by default; `additionalProperties: false` is an explicit closed-object rule.
sources.limits: Schema closure can prevent unreviewed fields but does not itself solve version migration or semantic truth.

sources.title: The import system: module cache
sources.supported_claim: Python checks writable `sys.modules` first; deleting a cache entry does not destroy references already held by other modules, and reimport may create a different module object.
sources.limits: Describes import semantics; test isolation choice still depends on the actual patched objects and consumers.

sources.title: How to monkeypatch/mock modules and environments
sources.supported_claim: pytest monkeypatch operations are undone at test/fixture teardown, and context scopes can undo earlier; direct global mutation without fixture tracking is not automatically repaired.
sources.limits: Fixture cleanup restores registered state only and cannot erase references leaked into other already-imported modules.

sources.title: TUF roles and metadata
sources.supported_claim: Trust decisions are purpose/role-bound and bind key thresholds, signatures, hashes, versions, and expiry; old metadata must be detected rather than silently promoted.
sources.limits: Software-update repository model; use as a design comparison for typed scope/time binding, not as a PolicyOS authority scheme or a call to adopt TUF.

sources.title: aiohttp client reference
sources.supported_claim: ClientSession owns connection pooling and supports context-managed closing; its recommended lifetime is application-level for ordinary use, not per request.
sources.limits: This only supports a bounded lifecycle repair if the original foreign task confirms session cleanup is its criterion; it does not establish that this foreign row has that criterion.

sources.title: Value of Information Analytical Methods: ISPOR VOI Analysis Emerging Good Practices Task Force, Report 2
sources.supported_claim: VOI compares expected decision-payoff improvement from information with acquisition/research cost; EVPI, EVPPI, EVSI and ENBS answer distinct questions, and population value depends on beneficiary population and useful horizon.
sources.limits: Health-technology-assessment application. Transfer the explicit decision model, assumptions, population, horizon, and cost separation; do not import its utility or monetary units into PolicyOS without an owner decision.

sources.title: ICH E9(R1) estimands and sensitivity analysis guideline
sources.supported_claim: A decision estimand needs explicit population, variable, intercurrent-event strategy, and population-level summary; comparability depends on the question and setting.
sources.limits: Clinical-trial-specific guidance; it is an example of fully specified estimands, not a universal PolicyOS metric contract.

sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.supported_claim: The Benjamini–Hochberg procedure controls FDR under its stated independent-test condition; repeated/exploratory discovery requires the declared testing family and dependence assumptions.
sources.limits: This result does not confer authority to any PolicyOS anomaly or solve longitudinal/repeated-look control without a fitted and justified procedure.

sources.title: PROV Model Primer
sources.supported_claim: PROV represents entities, activities, usage/generation, agents, and responsibility so a reader can trace artifact lineage and provenance assertions.
sources.limits: A provenance vocabulary records relationships; it does not decide whether an external function belongs in PolicyOS or whether evidence has admissible authority.

sources.title: WCAG Evaluation Methodology (WCAG-EM) 2.0
sources.supported_claim: A documented accessibility evaluation defines its scope, explores the product, selects a representative sample, evaluates it, and reports outcomes; sampling does not silently become whole-product inspection.
sources.limits: Accessibility methodology does not provide an independent countersign, nor replace the exact C13 print/content criteria or required qualified evaluator.

sources.title: Large-Scale Changes, Software Engineering at Google
sources.supported_claim: The described LSC process separates authorization, change creation, shard management, and cleanup; independent shards are tested and reviewed, while a train can run affected tests against the combined change set.
sources.limits: This is a Google process with dedicated tooling and different scale. Transfer the shard, owner, and combined-integration principles only; it does not establish PolicyOS throughput, resource limits, acceptance authority, or a need to build an LSC platform.

sources.title: Managing a merge queue
sources.supported_claim: Required checks are rerun for a temporary integration group based on the latest target branch and queued changes ahead of it; failed or conflicting groups are removed. A PR-head result alone is not the combined-tree result.
sources.limits: This is GitHub merge behavior, not a PolicyOS scheduler or a domain evidence rule. It supports binding final evidence to the integrated tree, not adopting a queue service.

sources.title: Merging stacked pull requests
sources.supported_claim: A dependent stack merges bottom-up; the status shown for a stack includes lower changes, and an intermediate change cannot be treated as an isolated integration when its lower dependencies are absent.
sources.limits: Stack semantics vary by host and merge strategy. Use this only to motivate explicit bases and dependency-aware review; PolicyOS keeps its existing root-only integration owner.

sources.title: Dismissing a pull request review
sources.supported_claim: GitHub treats a review as potentially outdated after the reviewed change changes and requires a reason when an administrator dismisses it.
sources.limits: The exact host behavior is not a universal review protocol. PolicyOS should carry review only across a proven unchanged scope and record why; it should not assume host approval state establishes semantic review.

sources.title: What to look for in a code review
sources.supported_claim: Reviewers should examine assigned changes in context and identify which portions they reviewed when review responsibility is split; qualified reviewers are needed for specialized concerns.
sources.limits: This is guidance for code review, not evidence of policy admissibility or competent closure of original obligations.

sources.title: SLSA v1.2 Build Provenance
sources.supported_claim: Build provenance binds an artifact to its build definition, external parameters, resolved dependencies, builder, invocation, and produced subject; consumers verify external parameters and dependency identity.
sources.limits: This is a software supply-chain specification. It informs source/input/run binding but does not prove a PolicyOS replay was semantically adequate, complete, or authorized.

sources.title: Reproducible Builds documentation
sources.supported_claim: Reproduction requires a strategy for recreating the build environment and managing sources of variance such as timestamps, locale, paths, and input order.
sources.limits: PolicyOS replay outputs may be nondeterministic and are not software binaries. Preserve exact conditions and outputs; do not promise bitwise replay equality absent a measured deterministic procedure.

sources.title: Dags: trigger rules
sources.supported_claim: Airflow distinguishes waiting for all upstream tasks to succeed from waiting for them merely to finish; some early-fire rules do not wait for every upstream task.
sources.limits: This is an orchestration example, not a PolicyOS dependency engine. It supports the conceptual distinction between starting independent shards, joining their terminal outcomes, and accepting their results; no Airflow component is proposed.

sources.title: OpenLineage custom facets
sources.supported_claim: Versioned custom facets extend a common event grammar; a same-name facet replaces the previous value.
sources.limits: Not an append-only authority ledger or independent evidence verifier.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg reliability
sources.supported_claim: Immutable metadata and atomic pointer replacement support optimistic table commits with validation.
sources.limits: One table commit is not a cross-store transaction or a rights/currentness proof.

sources.title: Jepsen consistency models
sources.supported_claim: Consistency properties are scoped; single-object linearizability does not imply multi-object serializability.
sources.limits: A model description is not a measured guarantee for the selected PolicyOS backend.

sources.title: Cedar policy validation
sources.supported_claim: Policy schema/type validation is distinct from evaluating a concrete authorization request.
sources.limits: No second policy engine is selected by this analogy.

sources.title: SLSA artifact verification
sources.supported_claim: Provenance verification binds artifact subject, expected builder and build claims.
sources.limits: Build provenance does not establish scientific correctness, legal authority or complete input custody.

sources.title: Materialize query optimization
sources.supported_claim: Projection/filter placement and retained state affect computation and memory costs.
sources.limits: Apply only with preserved semantics and measured workload; no benchmark transfer or time-rounding permission.

sources.title: Withheld propositions: WP-01/02/03 and activation boundaries
sources.supported_claim: WP-01 retains no posterior mutation pending its live producers and activation; WP-02 supplies no approved routine schedule.
